sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface incorporation into compact myelin confirmed by immunostaining (L4). In vitro and in vivo adhesion assays showed partial retention of P0-mediated adhesive function; the tagged protein also acted in a dominant-negative fashion on endogenous P0, indicating partial function perturbation (L5).
sites.rationale: L1 explicitly states the myc oligonucleotide was inserted at the MscI site in exon 2 corresponding to the NH2 terminus of the mature protein, recreating the signal peptide cleavage site in the full-length membrane-anchored construct. Python confirms residue 29 is A (last signal-peptide residue) and residue 30 is I (first mature extracellular residue), placing the junction at insert_after_residue=29. The extracellular domain spans residues 30–155 (126 residues), well clear of the TM boundary. Validation level is function_perturbed because adhesive function was only partially retained and a dominant-negative effect on endogenous P0 was observed. Full-length membrane-anchored P0 (mP0TOTmyc) with a myc epitope tag inserted in-frame at the MscI site in exon 2, downstream of the signal peptide coding sequence, placing the tag at the NH2 terminus of the mature extracellular domain; the signal peptide cleavage site was recreated. Expressed as a transgene in mice.

sources.claim: In mP 0 TOT(myc), an oligonucleotide encoding myc tag (5′-CCATTGAGCAAAAGCTCATTTCTGAAGAGGACTTGAATG-3′) was inserted in frame into the MscI site in P 0 exon 2, corresponding to the NH 2 terminus of the mature P 0 protein (see Fig. 1 ) and recreated the signal peptide cleavage site.

literature_notes: L2, L3, L4, L5, and L11 all corroborate the same myc-tag junction (after residue 29) and were considered; L1 was chosen as the primary clip because it gives the most explicit molecular description of the insertion site. L6/L7/L8/L10 describe a C-terminal HA tag: the C-terminus (residue 248) lies in the intracellular domain (180–248) and is therefore not a surface tag site; placed in other_positions. L9 describes EGFP-tagged P0 constructs but does not specify whether EGFP is at the N- or C-terminus; because P0 has both an extracellular N-terminus and an intracellular C-terminus, topology_derived reasoning cannot resolve the ambiguity, and no insert_after_residue can be pinned; this clip was therefore disqualified. L6 names G155, L158, and L162 as critical for MPZ–PMP22 interaction: G155 is only 1 residue from the TM boundary (below the ≥3-residue minimum) and L158/L162 are within the TM domain; all three are placed in other_positions as abrogates_function.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal HA tag on full-length MPZ used in co-immunoprecipitation experiments; residue 248 (K) falls within the intracellular domain (180–248), making this an intracellular tag, not a surface tag.
G155 confirmed critical for MPZ–PMP22 interaction in the context of C-terminally HA-tagged MPZ; also only 1 residue from the TM boundary, below the ≥3-residue minimum for a surface tag.
L158 confirmed critical for MPZ–PMP22 interaction; residue 158 lies within the TM domain (156–179) and is not accessible on the extracellular surface.
L162 confirmed critical for MPZ–PMP22 interaction; residue 162 lies within the TM domain (156–179) and is not accessible on the extracellular surface.
